title: A protein-language model enabled selective β-catenin degraders in preclinical tests
summary: A protein-language model helped design candidate binders used in programmable degraders. Selected designs reduced abnormal β-catenin in cell experiments, and one candidate was tested in mice. These preclinical results do not establish human safety or therapeutic efficacy.
ai_technology: SaLT&PepPr, a protein-language-model-based algorithm, designed candidate β-catenin-binding peptides.
organization: Robert F. Smith School of Chemical and Biomolecular Engineering, Cornell University, Ithaca, NY, USA

evidence.tested: Selected model-designed candidates were evaluated in cell experiments and a mouse study; the result is preclinical.
evidence.unknown: No human safety or therapeutic-efficacy evidence is reported.
evidence.ai_role: A protein-language-model-based algorithm designed candidate binders that enabled a selective-degrader study.

source_review.scope: Primary full-text review as recorded in case evidence; record-level claim and attribution review.
